title: Late Charges on Overdue Remittances — Paystride Earned Wage Access Program Agreement
content:
This text governs late charges under the Paystride Earned Wage Access Program Agreement. Two of its clauses, marked below, are no longer in force.

**1. Overdue items (no longer in force).** The clause "An overdue item is a deduction schedule, or an employer-liable shortfall notice, whose open amount remains after its due date." is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current basis.

**2. Grace.** A late charge is assessed only once the tier's late-charge grace, in business days, has passed since the item's due date. Business days are Monday through Friday excluding Federal Reserve holidays, counted from the day after the due date; the grace has passed on the day that completes that number of business days, and a late charge may be assessed from that day on, never earlier. The due date is the one recorded on the schedule or notice.

**3. Late-charge periods.** Once the grace has passed, each late-charge period of the tier's late-charge period length in calendar days begins on the due date, so the second period begins on the due date plus that number of days. An overdue item incurs at most one late charge per late-charge period.

**4. Amount (no longer in force).** The clause "The late charge for a period is the greater of the minimum late charge and the late charge rate of the item's open amount on the first day of that period, rounded to the nearest cent;" is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current basis.

**5. Booking.** A late charge points to the item it charges, carries the late charge invoice line, and is due the tier's invoice payment term, in calendar days, after it is booked. Provider-absorbed amounts are never charged.

**6. Courtesy waiver.** A late charge may be waived as a courtesy, by a late-charge-waiver credit memo, only while the number of late-charge-waiver credit memos on the agreement in the 365 calendar days ending today is below the tier's courtesy waiver allowance; a tier allowing none grants none.

**7. Returned remittances.** A late charge caused by a returned remittance runs from the schedule's original due date.

## Grace and periods illustrated (hypothetical, two-business-day grace, 30-day periods, no holidays)

| Item due on | Grace passed on | Second period begins |
|---|---|---|
| a Monday | the Wednesday of that week | 30 calendar days after that Monday |
| a Friday | the Tuesday of the following week | 30 calendar days after that Friday |

For the item due on a Monday, no late charge may yet be assessed on the Tuesday; from the Wednesday one may, and no second one within the same period.

## Courtesy waiver illustrated (hypothetical)

On a tier allowing one waiver in any rolling 365 days, a waiver booked 200 days ago leaves no room for another today; once that waiver is more than 365 days old, a new one may be granted.

superseded_clauses: An overdue item is a deduction schedule, or an employer-liable shortfall notice, whose open amount remains after its due_date.
